item.text:
**Bottom line**  
Tinubu in 2024 shows **some real use of measurement and correction**, especially through KPI reporting, technocratic coordination, targeted social programs, and procurement reform. But the record is **still mixed** because much of the correction was reactive, several key systems remained opaque or punitive, and I did not find strong evidence of a mature, public service-delivery dashboard culture across health, water, sanitation, or housing.

**Accepted claims**
- **President Tinubu directs expeditious processing of welfare benefits, demands monthly KPI reports** | State House | 2024-02-22 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-expeditious-processing-of-welfare-benefits-demands-monthly-kpi-reports/)  
  Tinubu ordered faster welfare delivery and explicit monthly KPI reporting for vulnerable-citizen interventions. This is direct evidence of measurement and corrective management, not just rhetoric.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.4, 6B.3

- **President Tinubu establishes comprehensive economic coordination and planning system for Nigeria** | State House | 2024-03-27 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-comprehensive-economic-coordination-and-planning-system-for-nigeria/)  
  PECC/EET put the finance minister, CBN governor, economists, and private-sector figures at the center of emergency coordination. That is strong evidence of technocratic, evidence-aware governance rather than ad hoc patronage.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.4

- **With good governance and commitment, we must overcome old subsidy beneficiaries** | State House | 2024-03-15 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/with-good-governance-and-commitment-we-must-overcomee-old-subsidy-benificiaries-president-tinubu/)  
  Tinubu tied subsidy reform to targeted relief using NIN data, plus student loans, consumer credit, and social welfare. This supports a diagnosis-driven, targeted-correction approach.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.2, 6B.3

- **The IMF said Tinubu’s government paired austerity with cereals, subsidized fertilizer, wage awards, and diesel VAT suspension** | IMF | 2024-02-09 | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/02/09/pr2443-nigeria-imf-exec-board-concludes-pfa)  
  The IMF described a coherent stabilization package with palliatives meant to soften reform shock. That is good evidence of policy correction informed by economic diagnosis.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.2

- **President Tinubu establishes national education data system and approves skill development, teacher training and support nationwide** | State House | 2024-04-18 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-establishes-national-education-data-system-and-approves-skill-development-for-all-levels-of-education-teachers-training-and-support-nationwide/)  
  The national education data repository and out-of-school-children measures are direct evidence of measurement infrastructure in service delivery.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.2, 6B.3

- **President Tinubu directs reorganisation of the Bureau of Public Procurement** | State House | 2024-06-15 | [URL](https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-directs-reorganisation-of-the-bureau-of-public-procurement/)  
  Procurement reform is a concrete transparency move aimed at value for money and cleaner spending rules. That matters for service delivery because it targets a classic bottleneck.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.4

- **World Bank approves new financing for Nigeria to improve health outcomes, safety of dams and irrigation services** | World Bank | 2024-09-26 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/09/26/world-bank-approves-new-financing-for-nigeria-to-improve-health-outcomes-safety-of-dams-and-irrigation-services)  
  The package explicitly targeted governance bottlenecks in health, education, and resilience infrastructure. This supports the view that service delivery was being approached through measurable institutional fixes.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.2, 6B.3

- **Tinubu orders probe of security agents involved in arrest, detention of minors** | TheCable | 2024-11-04 | [URL](https://www.thecable.ng/tinubu-orders-probe-of-security-agents-involved-in-arrest-detention-of-minors/)  
  After public backlash, Tinubu ordered an investigation into arrests and treatment of minors, with possible discipline for officers. This is the clearest evidence of transparent correction, but it came late and was reactive.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.3

- **UNICEF welcomes President Tinubu’s order for immediate release of detained children** | UNICEF Nigeria | 2024-11-05 | [URL](https://www.unicef.org/nigeria/press-releases/unicef-welcomes-president-tinubus-order-immediate-release-detained-children)  
  UNICEF corroborated the release of detained children and young people. This strengthens the corrective-action record, but it still looks like damage control rather than a standing accountability system.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.3

- **World Bank says reforms improved macro stability, but inflation remained high and execution was incomplete** | World Bank | 2024-10-17 | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/17/nigeria-staying-the-course-on-reforms-progress-amidst-challenges)  
  The Bank’s own caveat shows the administration had not yet turned reform intent into broadly visible service-delivery gains. It is positive on trajectory, but weak on outcome proof.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.2

**Counterevidence**
- **Nigeria has detained journalist who reported on corruption in widening crackdown** | Reuters via GPB | 2024-05-09 | [URL](https://www.gpb.org/news/2024/05/09/nigeria-has-detained-journalist-who-reported-on-corruption-in-widening-crackdown)  
  Detaining a journalist over corruption reporting weakens the feedback loop needed for transparent correction and service-delivery oversight.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.4

- **Nigeria police charge 4 journalists with cybercrimes for corruption reporting** | CPJ | 2024-10-03 | [URL](https://cpj.org/2024/10/nigeria-police-charge-4-journalists-with-cybercrimes-for-corruption-reporting/)  
  Continued use of cybercrime charges against journalists suggests a punitive information environment, which is bad evidence for open measurement and correction.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.4

- **Freedom House, Nigeria: Freedom on the Net 2024** | Freedom House | 2024 | [URL](https://freedomhouse.org/country/nigeria/freedom-net/2024)  
  Freedom House describes cybercrime-law pressure, monitoring of “false information,” blocking powers, and continued harassment of journalists. That undercuts claims of a transparent correction culture.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.4

- **Nigeria police used excessive force to violently quash #EndBadGovernance protests** | Amnesty International | 2024-11-28 | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/nigeria-police-used-excessive-force-to-violently-quash-endbadgovernance-protests/)  
  When welfare grievances surfaced at scale, the state responded coercively, with killings and mass detentions rather than visible policy correction.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.3

- **Nigeria charges protesters with treason and mutiny** | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-09-02 | [URL](https://theprint.in/world/nigeria-charges-protesters-with-treason-inciting-military/2249248/)  
  The treason/mutiny framing shows legal escalation rather than transparent learning from public distress.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.3

- **FG spent N63.6bn on military equipment in seven months, report says** | Punch | 2024-08-17 | [URL](https://punchng.com/fg-spent-n63-6bn-on-military-equipment-in-seven-months-report/)  
  Weakly disclosed security spending raises transparency concerns and makes it harder to tell whether public funds were being used with disciplined monitoring.  
  QIDs: 6B.5, 6B.4

**Search gap**
- I found **little direct public evidence of routine service-delivery dashboards or published scorecards** in health, water, sanitation, or housing.
- The strongest measurement evidence is in **macro coordination, education data, and procurement reform**, not in sector-by-sector outcome tracking.
- The strongest correction evidence is **reactive** and centered on protest-related abuses, not on a visible, iterative correction loop for ordinary service delivery.
